question.worked_solution:
The sum to infinity ${S}_{\infty }$ of a geometric series is given by

$$
{S}_{\infty }=\frac{{a}_{1}}{1-r},\,|r|<1.
$$

The first term is

$$
{a}_{1}=6(0.5)^{2(1)}=6(0.5)^{2}=6(0.25)=1.5,
$$

and the second term is

$$
{a}_{2}=6(0.5)^{2(2)}=6(0.5)^{4}.
$$

Therefore, the common ratio is

$$
r=\frac{{a}_{2}}{{a}_{1}}=\frac{6(0.5)^{4}}{6(0.5)^{2}}=(0.5)^{2}=0.25.
$$

So, the sum of the series is

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }6(0.5)^{2n} & =\frac{{a}_{1}}{1-r} \\  & =\frac{1.5}{1-0.25} \\  & =\frac{1.5}{0.75} \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$
